title: Quantized allocator thrash caused serving instability and subtle eval drift
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: Summary: During a production deployment of an int8-quantized family of chat models we observed a cluster-wide instability window (2026-02-17 ~09:12-09:58 UTC) where a subset of serving nodes entered repeated OOM/restart loops. The instability manifested as increased tail-latency, routing fallbacks to higher-precision kernels, and a measurable but subtle drop in certain eval prompt pass-rates for long-context conversational tests. This ticket captures the triage, root cause analysis, short-term mitigations, and proposed long-term remediations.
timeline: 2026-02-17 09:10 UTC - Canary rollout of runtime-1.22 with new allocator heuristics began.
2026-02-17 09:12 UTC - Pager alerts: Node group quant-gpu-pool-3 reported OOMs and K8s restarts; autoscaler started draining.
2026-02-17 09:20 UTC - Traffic routing moved to standby pool; partial degradation persisted for ~30 minutes.
2026-02-17 09:45 UTC - Observed increased frequency of kernel fallbacks to fp16 paths for attention ops (telemetry: kernel_fallback_rate spike +6x).
2026-02-17 09:58 UTC - Hotfix: rollout paused and runtime reverted to runtime-1.21; immediate reduction in OOM loops observed.
2026-02-18 10:00 UTC - Post-incident logging captures were collected and initial RCA workshop held.
2026-02-20 11:30 UTC - Reproduced allocator thrash locally with synthetic load pattern (small batch, varied sequence length).
root_cause: A combination of a new allocator compaction heuristic in runtime-1.22 and an interaction with int8 quantized weight layout caused frequent tiny free/alloc cycles under workloads dominated by many small batches and variable sequence lengths. The allocator's compaction triggered repeated KV cache evictions and micro-migrations of tensors, increasing fragmentation and GPU memory churn. The churn caused opportunistic kernel selector to detect insufficient contiguous memory and route some ops to alternative (higher-precision) kernels; those alternative kernels exposed a numeric path with marginal accuracy differences on a few eval cases. Canary coverage missed the long-tail small-batch+long-seq workload pattern and allocator metrics were not instrumented at the granularity needed to catch the thrash before customer impact.
mitigation: Reverted runtime to 1.21 in prod (done 2026-02-17) to stop the OOM loop.
Applied a temporary allocator gating flag that disables the compaction heuristic for quantized models (flag: ALLOC_GC_DISABLE_COMPACT=true) across Dedicated pools.
Increased canary traffic diversity to include small-batch long-context sequences for future rollouts.
Added temporary autoscaler override to preserve a reserve pool of nodes for fallback capacity during rollouts.
Rolled forward a minor allocator patch (branch: hotfix/alloc-stability-97456) to staging for verification before longterm rollout.
action_items: (A1) Add allocator-level telemetry: track allocation size histogram, compaction triggers, and fragmentation ratio per model type. Owner: Marco Chen. ETA: 2 wks.
(A2) Expand canary suite: add long-context small-batch scenario and targeted eval prompts that previously showed drift. Owner: Riley Gomez (Evals). ETA: 1 week.
(A3) Implement allocator compaction safety checks: disallow compaction when active KV cache occupancy > 70% for quantized models. Owner: Lina Ortega. ETA: 3 wks.
(A4) Add deterministic repro harness for allocator thrash: synthetic harness that simulates many small batches and mixed seq-lengths to run in CI nightly. Owner: QA team. ETA: 2 wks.

(A5) Audit kernel selector fallbacks: ensure numeric-path-conservatism for fallback kernels; add unit tests comparing outputs on eval suites before allowing automatic fallback. Owner: Runtime-ops. ETA: 4 wks.
(A6) Postmortem doc & blameless review session with SRE, Runtime, Evals and Product. Owner: Aisha Kapoor. ETA: 1 week.
(A7) Release readiness checklist update: include allocator metric thresholds and canary diversity validation. Owner: PM. ETA: 1 week.
(A8) Backfill historical telemetry for last 90 days to detect prior low-level occurrences. Owner: Observability. ETA: 3 wks.
(A9) Coordinate customer communication for impacted enterprise tenants (support tracked separately). Owner: Customer Success. ETA: 3 days.
(A10) Evaluate long-term allocator redesign (slab + segregated cache for KV tensors) and include in roadmap if cost-benefit positive. Owner: Runtime-architecture. ETA: discovery by next quarter.
(A11) Create an automated rollback trigger during rollout if allocator compaction events exceed threshold X within 10 minutes. Owner: Deploy infra. ETA: 2 wks.
resolution_summary: Immediate: runtime rollback to 1.21 and gating flag stopped the OOM/restart loops. Short-term: hotfix branch validated in staging and a gated rollout plan was prepared. Long-term: telemetry and allocator-safety changes are scheduled; canary expansion and repro harness will prevent regression recurrence and catch subtle eval drift earlier.
postmortem_notes: Key takeaways: 1) allocator heuristics can have outsized effects when combined with quantized memory layouts and KV cache eviction patterns; 2) canary tests must include realistic workload permutations, not just average-case traffic; 3) fallback kernel selection must be treated as a potentially high-risk path for quality drift and gated accordingly. We will run a blameless retro on 2026-03-01 to surface process gaps and update the rollout checklist.
